title: Docs: update public/internal docs for overload errors + client retry guidance (coordinate with DevEx)
creator: Elliot Price
description:
Goal
Update public + internal documentation to reflect new overload-protection behavior (circuit breakers + load shedding) with stable error semantics and clear client retry guidance. Coordinate with DevEx/SDKs so the docs match the actual error payload + headers across REST and OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

Context
As we roll out layered overload protection (edge admission control, routing breaker evaluation, runtime bounded queues/shed points), customers will see a higher fraction of deterministic 429/503 responses with Redwood-specific error codes and Retry-After guidance instead of ambiguous timeouts/5xx. Docs must:
- Make the behavior predictable and non-alarming
- Reduce support load by giving clear retry/backoff guidance
- Preserve compatibility expectations for OpenAI-compatible clients

Deliverables
1) Public docs (redwood-docs)
- New/updated page: “Overload errors and retry guidance”
  - When you may see overload errors (spikes, burst traffic, regional capacity constraints)
  - Status code mapping principles (429 vs 503) with examples
  - Headers to expect: Retry-After (seconds), request-id/trace correlation
  - Error body shape (Redwood API + OpenAI-compat)
  - Recommended client behavior: exponential backoff with jitter, respect Retry-After, cap total attempts, avoid parallel retry storms
  - Streaming note: partial streams/disconnects and safe retry pattern (idempotency guidance where applicable)
- FAQ section
  - Do overload responses count toward billing/usage?
  - How to tune retries for batch jobs vs interactive traffic
  - How Dedicated differs from Hosted (Dedicated may shed later/with different capacity guarantees; customers should still implement retry)

2) Internal docs (Confluence)
- Add a short internal “support + oncall quick explainer” that mirrors the public page, but includes:
  - How to interpret error codes + where to check dashboards
  - Standard support macros / response snippets
  - When to escalate vs when to recommend client-side changes

3) DevEx / SDK alignment
- Verify SDK error objects surface:
  - Redwood error code
  - Retry-After
  - A structured “should_retry” hint (if implemented) doesn’t contradict docs
- Ensure examples in docs match Python/TS/Go examples (or link to SDK docs/examples).

Acceptance criteria
- Public docs merged and published prior to expanding canary beyond initial region/model set.
- Docs include at least 3 worked examples:
  - 429 with Retry-After
  - 503 with Retry-After
  - OpenAI-compat error object example (non-streaming)
- Retry guidance explicitly warns against immediate tight-loop retries and recommends jitter.
- Dedicated vs Hosted callout is reviewed by PM (Lauren Bishop + Nikhil Sharma) for correctness.
- Support macro and internal guide reviewed by Dev Patel/Owen Phillips.

References
- ADR: Overload error taxonomy + HTTP mapping (Confluence ADR-0147)
- Support guidance draft: overload errors and client retry guidance (Confluence)
- Implementation tickets: ENG-4823 (standardized error payload + headers), ENG-4836 (SDK surfacing)
- Launch planning: PM-912

Risks / gotchas to address in wording
- Avoid implying a hard SLA guarantee that “retries will always succeed”
- Avoid encouraging unlimited retries
- Ensure we distinguish overload-protected errors (expected under load) vs internal failures (unexpected)
- Keep language consistent with OpenAI-compatible endpoint expectations (don’t break client parsing)

Owner notes
Wei to drive the public page; Elliot to coordinate review + internal Confluence updates with Support/Oncall enablement.

comments: 2025-12-11 (Elliot Price): Created for docs workstream. Please keep wording strictly aligned to ADR-0147. Biggest theme from SUP-3928/SUP-3961 is customers seeing mixed 500/502/503 + unclear retries. We need a single canonical page we can point to.

2025-12-13 (Wei Chen): Draft outline ready. Waiting on final error payload schema from ENG-4823 so examples match the actual JSON shape + OpenAI-compat mapping. In the meantime, I’ll write retry guidance + streaming notes.

2025-12-16 (Monica Patel): SDKs will surface Retry-After and Redwood error codes. We should avoid promising a `should_retry` boolean until it lands everywhere. Recommend docs say: “If Retry-After present, prefer it; otherwise use exponential backoff with jitter.”

2025-12-19 (Dev Patel): Support asks that we explicitly answer “does this count against billing?” and “why did this start happening now?” (re: rollout). Suggest adding a short paragraph explaining overload protection is intentional to prevent cascading failures and improves overall availability.

2026-01-03 (Wei Chen): Public docs draft is up in redwood-docs PR #912. Includes 429/503 examples and OpenAI-compat example. Added guidance: cap attempts (e.g., 5), honor Retry-After, jitter, and avoid synchronized retries across workers. Added streaming note: retry at request-level, not mid-stream; expect occasional disconnects under load.

2026-01-06 (Henry Cho): Requested we clarify 429 vs 503 language: 429 is “temporarily overloaded / request not admitted” and 503 is “temporarily unavailable for the chosen model/region/tier.” Also please add a short section: “What you can do: reduce concurrency, shorten prompts, use batching, consider Dedicated.”

2026-01-08 (Lauren Bishop): Dedicated callout: OK to say Dedicated has reserved capacity and different SLOs, but still may shed if customer exceeds contracted concurrency or during maintenance/failover. Avoid implying Dedicated never returns 429/503.

2026-01-12 (Wei Chen): Updated per PM feedback. Added a table: condition → code → recommended client action. Also added a disclaimer: overload responses are not billed as successful tokens; link to billing FAQ (pending).
2026-01-15 (Sergio Costa): Please include link to status page and guidance: if prolonged elevated shed rates occur, check status page first; include request-id when contacting support.
2026-01-17 (Elliot Price): Internal Confluence page created: “Hosted API overload errors: support/oncall quick explainer” with macros and escalation criteria. Sent to Support for review.

2026-01-22 (Wei Chen): PR #912 merged and published. Internal page reviewed by Dev Patel/Owen Phillips. Marking ENG-4832 Done. Follow-up: ensure billing FAQ link stays current once Cole posts the official billing note.
